subject: physics
title: Momentum, Impulse and Collisions
welcome_lead: Conserve momentum through explosions and collisions, and use impulse to handle changing forces.
meta_desc: A-Level Mechanics adventure on momentum, impulse and collision analysis.
final_note: Momentum is always conserved in closed systems — kinetic energy only sometimes.

concepts.def: Product of mass and velocity: p = mv.
Change in momentum: J = F·t = Δp.
Collision where kinetic energy is conserved.
Collision losing kinetic energy (often to heat).
Total momentum before equals total after.

walkthroughs.body_html: Impulse J = F·Δt = Δp = m(v - u). A large force for short time and a small force for long time can give the same impulse — that's why crumple zones work.
m1 u1 + m2 u2 = m1 v1 + m2 v2. Treat directions with signs. For perfectly inelastic: m1 u1 + m2 u2 = (m1+m2) v.
Calculate ½mv² before and after. If KE is conserved the collision is elastic. If KE drops, energy went to deformation, heat or sound.

mcqs.q: Which quantity is always conserved in a collision (no external forces)?

numericals.q: 5 kg trolley at 4 m/s hits stationary 5 kg trolley, sticks. Final speed (m/s)?

free_texts.q: What is the SI unit of momentum?
